newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips end higher in light pre-Christmas trading.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips end higher in light pre-Christmas trading.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks ended an abbreviated trading session with solid gains Tuesday as investors scooped up big-name stocks and rushed off to celebrate the Christmas holiday.

The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 33.83 points at 6,522.85. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,295 to 921 on very light volume of 167 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The stock market closed early at 1 p.m. EST/1800 GMT and will be shut Wednesday, Christmas day.

"It's the last day for Christmas shopping and the last day of trading before Christmas. We have a holiday environment with much of the tax-selling apparently behind us," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
"Santa is surprising us again," he said. "The traditional Christmas rally is at hand."

The market's rally bode well for Wall Street's prospects according to the old saying -- "If Santa should fail to call, bears could come to Broad and Wall," the streets that are the site of the New York Stock Exchange.

As for the Dow's action, David Kelly, senior economist with Primark Decision Economics, said, "It's not a sign of people rooting out value in smaller companies, it's just money looking for a safe home."

A rebound in technology stocks helped to lead the overall market higher. Compaq rose 1-7/8 to 74-5/8, Seagate added 2-1/8 to 40-1/8, International Business Machines Corp. was up 1-3/4 to 155-7/8 and Intel rose 3-1/4 to 135-1/2.
Among individual stocks, Motorola rose 1-5/8 to 60-1/2. Lehman Brothers called Motorola the "best idea for 1997 in the wireless communications equipment industry."

KCS Energy rallied 7-7/8 to 37-5/8 on news that it settled all litigation with Tennessee Gas Pipeline. KCS said 1997 and 1998 earnings will suffer from the settlement that calls for the companies to end their contract two years ahead of schedule.
Digi International slumped 3-7/8 to 8-7/8. It warned that its first-quarter earnings will fall short of expectations.
TRO Learning Inc. plunged 6-3/4 to 10-1/2 after the maker of educational computer software reported disappointing earnings.
The Nasdaq Composite index closed 8.11 points higher at 1,287.63.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 4.11 to 751.03. The American Stock Exchange index edged up 0.37 to 581.35.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.71 to 395.00. The average share was up 18 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,231.993 up 30.437 or 0.42 percent.
